## FIX 1 — Opus stand-ins. SOUND, simplest sufficient.

**Ran:** `claude -p "Reply with exactly: OK" --model opus --setting-sources "" ...` under the shim's exact flag set → `OK`, rc 0 (CLI 2.1.220). The string resolves and dispatches. `run_simulated_experiment` passes `args.model` through to `SHIM.install` (line 290) — the flag is live end to end.

**Attack answered:** cost is subscription ($0, stated); wall-clock risk is already handled — timeout was raised to 900 s with raise-on-timeout telemetry before this change, and Opus being slower only consumes that budget, it can't silently corrupt a run. No written rationale for Sonnet exists anywhere I could find; the founder ruling is quoted in-line.

Either add the two-line `--model` argument or delete the complaint; a comment that names a defect the fix didn't repair will be quoted later as if it had been.

## FIX 2 — calibration + tagger flags. Wiring sound; the CLAIM is false — there IS a third gate.

**Ran:** the project's own `prove_latent_tagger_reaches_gate.py`. Arm C — "both ON (the mechanism live)" — demotes **0 of 3**, verdict unchanged from arm A. The eligible entry is skipped with "no worked proof that reproduces."

The third gate is `severity_is_proven` (runner:6554, interlock added 2026-09-06, *after* the proof tool was written): demotion additionally requires a stamped severity proof with status PASS/WARN — produced only when the model supplies a worked R_k derivation that recomputes — or `latent_source == "external"`. So enabling both flags makes the *sweep* execute; the *demotion* still cannot, unless the seats also emit (a) an explicit reachability/latency field (0 of 293 archival findings carry one, per the tool's own footer) and (b) a reproducing R_k proof. The rehearsal as shipped still rehearses a no-op.

**Config parity:** checked all 46 shipped `exp*_configs/*.json` by script — none sets either flag, so paid runs have them OFF. Default-ON is a *stated* divergence and acceptable as stress-test; the failure is only that it doesn't yet stress anything.

**Fix:** no new mechanism needed. (1) Update the proof tool's fixture: give C2 `"severity_proof": {"status": "PASS"}` so arm C demonstrates the chain again — right now the tool's prose claims a demonstration its own output refutes. (2) Add one sentence to the harness comment naming the proof requirement as the third condition, so the next reader doesn't rediscover it. The `rk_proof_requests_for_next_round` feedback channel already exists to elicit proofs from round 1 — the supply side needs no new machinery either.

## FIX 3 — round-0 deferral. SOUND, simplest sufficient, and I found the remaining cause.

**Deferral doesn't block forever — traced:** `routing_deferred` is written at 5345 and read *nowhere* (grep: single site, whole repo). The branch leaves `escalated=True`, and `apply_falsifier_verdicts` re-stamps UNTOOLABLE→escalated every round, so the entry re-enters the full ladder each round. Deferred criticals lack `irreducible_escalation`, so `unverified_critical_count` (skip at 1998 applies only to the irreducible flag) keeps counting them — they block convergence until assessed. Fail-safe, exactly as claimed. Cost worth stating: a never-assessed critical now burns a full 6-rung ladder *every* round on a paid panel; bounded by max_rounds, acceptable.

**Predicate:** both fields exist and are written by the assessing paths — no cheaper property does the job (`falsifier_verdict=="UNTOOLABLE"` covers only half). One asymmetry: `sk_evaluated` is stamped only in the ADMISSIBLE branch (10708), so a fix that S_k *evaluated and REJECTED* on a falsifier-less finding reads as "never assessed." Wrong label, fail-safe direction; move the stamp above the tristate split if precision matters.

**All three Wilson intervals reproduce exactly** (33/83→[29.9, 50.5], 49/83→[48.3, 69.0], 19/83→[15.2, 33.0]; derived, not trusted).

**The remaining cause — replayed the archive myself.** In the worst alarm run (exp53 2026-08-01): 20 escalations, 7 deferred, **7 criticals remain irreducible → alarm still fires**. Every surviving flagged entry carries `falsifier_verdict = ERROR` — the instrument *ran and crashed*, so the predicate correctly doesn't defer them — and one falsifier body appears **5× byte-identical** among the 7 (dup groups [5,1,1] = **3 distinct defects**). The alarm counts items, not defects: six seats duplicating one crashing falsifier clears bound 2 by multiplicity alone. **Fix:** make `irreducible_queue_count` count *distinct clusters*, using the already-calibrated Jaccard/STEM-signature instrument the absorb path trusts (7→3 in exp53). Second-order: ERROR-class falsifiers on prose targets are the feedstock; that is the S_k/prose instrument problem the alarm bundle already names, not a routing problem.

## FIX 4 — corrected S\* live. Core SOUND; the fallback is NOT, and there's a simpler gate.

**Ran (all derived by execution):** operating point reproduces exactly — corrected rejects sk=0.30 at floor 0.504931 where shipped passed at 0.0. My 1425-point grid: **0 looser, 180 stricter** — same shape as the stated 0/215. Downstream: `s_star` lands only in `sk_result` records and log lines; no code consumer expects the shipped value (grep across bench/explorer/scripts: none).

**The fallback fails in the permissive direction, measured:** on a 4800-cell sweep of the None region, **489 cells admit a fix that `compute_rk` shows RAISES residual risk** (no break-even exists precisely because *every* s does harm — low-R regimes where any modification injects risk; shipped s_star clamps to ≤ sk and passes). And at R=1 — the exact value the non-finite guard coerces a corrupt R to — the fallback returns `(True, 0.0)`: pass everything. That contradicts `sk_break_even`'s own docstring, ten lines above, which returns None *specifically so that* a corrupt input cannot become a maximally permissive gate. None cases enumerated: R=1 (polynomial identically zero), ν_b=1, disc<0, no root in [0,1] (these are the 489), R=0 and ν_b+ν_f=0 (fall conservative).

**The fix — simplest sufficient, verified:** the gate needs no root-finding and no fallback. Break-even is *defined* by `compute_rk(R,q,s) == R`; the gate only needs the sign at the sk under test:

```python
passes = compute_rk(R_old, q, sk, nu_b, nu_f) <= R_old   # fix must not raise risk
```

`compute_rk` already exists, is trusted, and carries the non-finite guard. Verified: agrees with the corrected gate at **all 1125 non-None grid points (0 mismatches)** and correctly rejects all 489 harmful fallback admissions. Keep `sk_break_even` purely to *record* s_star. This deletes the degenerate machinery instead of patching it — the origin-case shape: the hard question ("where is the root?") never needed answering; the cheap question ("does this sk raise risk?") was already computable.

## FIX 5 — key register. One regression CONFIRMED by execution; and yes, the seal should refuse.

**(a) Word-split regression.** Built a scoring.env with a legacy store named `legacy with space` holding `ft-001_KEY.json` and an unclassifiable file. `register` **silently omitted the entire store** — not in the register, no error — while `status` (fixed for exactly this class on 2026-09-06) correctly reported both files. Cause: `register` line 186 expands `${CDSFL_LEGACY_STORES}` unquoted; `vault`'s fold loop (line 75) has the same split, so a space-path legacy store is silently *not folded* at seal time. The codebase's own comment says the canonical path contains a space ("Application Support"). This is the 2026-09-06 status() bug reintroduced in the 2026-09-07 function beside it. **Fix:** feed both loops by redirection, the pattern status() already establishes:
```sh
while IFS= read -r _loc; do [ -n "$_loc" ] || continue; ...; done <<EOF
$STORE
${CDSFL_LEGACY_STORES:-}
EOF
```

**(b) UNCLASSIFIED.** The placeholder is not strong enough, and here is the argument rather than the assertion: filenames survive in the plaintext manifest, so `describe` *can* be extended and the register regenerated later — the loss is bounded to what the filename fails to convey. But that bounded loss is precisely the failure already realised: the 174,112-byte pre-manifest archive whose contents are "currently unknowable without opening it." Seal time is the unique enforcement point — the only moment a human is guaranteed present (typing the passphrase) while the content is still readable to check. Currently `vault` never calls `describe` or `register` at all; the record exists only if the operator remembers a separate command, which is this project's most-documented failure class. **Fix:** in `vault()`, before `tar`, run every file-to-be-sealed through `describe`; if any returns UNCLASSIFIED, print the list and `exit 1` ("classify it — one line in the case statement — then reseal"), and write the register as part of sealing. Extends the two functions that exist; no override flag needed, because the remedy is a one-line edit.
